text:
Samir: Quick heads up — ran a short burst profile against canary yesterday. Host CPU 95p spikes on ~64-token short requests. Looks like parsing + tokenization + small KV serializations are dominating. :eyes:
Emily: Do you have the profile?
Samir: Pasted top stacks below (very small sample, but consistent):
```
parse_request     1.25ms
http_decode       0.62ms
tokenize          0.98ms
kv_serialize      2.80ms
stream_chunking   0.45ms
grpc_encode       0.70ms
other_syscalls    0.15ms
```
Jordan: that kv_serialize number is nasty for tiny requests. Is that the JSON path or binary k/v form?
Samir: Binary protobuf path — small keys, but we do a per-request memcpy + zlib compress for telemetry.
Marta: Are we compressing on host for all tiers? Thought we only did for long responses.
Samir: It was enabled by default in the ingress shim after the 3.2 rollout. Short bursts hit it heavily.
Emily: Repro steps? I can run a lean microbench.
Samir: curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' http://ingress-canary:8080/v1/gen?model=gpt-small --repeat 500 --concurrency 8
Emily: I'll try toggling two things: (1) disable per-request kv compress, (2) short-circuit tokenizer preparse for single-token prompts.
Jordan: Also consider a fast-path in request parser: if body < 256b and no functions field, skip full JSON->proto conversion and use a memview. Cuts parse_request in half in our earlier bench.
Marta: For streaming chunking: can we send raw token frames instead of re-encoding into gRPC every time? Even batching 8 frames into one gRPC message could help.
Samir: I prototyped a small coalescer. When enabled, grpc_encode drops from 0.7ms->0.12ms and stream_chunking cost amortizes.
infra-bot: Deployed patch 2026-11-12T09:42:00Z to ingress-canary (coalescer=off by default).
Emily: Ran microbench locally: disabling kv compress -> kv_serialize 2.80ms -> 0.42ms, end-to-end p95 down ~18%.
Jordan: Nice. Next: add a heuristic to only compress KV if response size > 2KB or latency budget > 200ms. Also add a batching heuristic in the host to aggregate tiny parses into a single parse task for concurrent inflight requests.
Marta: I can add a simple counter in the parser to coalesce <1ms requests every 5ms window. Might add 1-2ms tail but reduce overall CPU churn.
Samir: Let's ship two toggles to canary: kv_compress_threshold=2048, parser_coalesce_window_ms=5, stream_coalesce_batch=8. Rolling to canary now.
Emily: Leaving notes in perf doc: https://perf.redwood.internal/report/1857 — includes before/after flamegraphs and the microbench script.
Jordan: If we get good numbers on canary, we should backport to dedicated pools as a config flag only (customers can opt-in).
Samir: Agreed. Will follow up with a short post in #eng-runtime with perf numbers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
